description: CHARACTERIZATION FIXTURE for saga #811 (issue #816): this records that `check()` is SILENT here today. It asserts an EMPTY diagnostics list, and that emptiness is the point — do not read it as a statement about the contract, because the contract now says the opposite. The #814 ruling has since MERGED, and it decides this case against today's behaviour: spec/tooling.md:193 makes a built-in Command in value position statically decidable and MUST-reportable at the checker as `ol-no-output`, naming `wait forward 5`, `repeat forward 5 [ … ]` and `right forward 5` explicitly, and spec/error-model.md:114 gives that code stage `semantic` for a built-in. So this fixture must FLIP — gaining one `ol-no-output` — when #815 implements the rule; it is no longer conditional on which mechanism is chosen. Fault shape B — a KNOWN command used in VALUE position (issue #716, re-parented under saga #811). This is a DIFFERENT fault from shape A and the fixtures record it separately on purpose. Here `check()` is CLEAN, not merely unconsulted: `forward` resolves fine once `turtle-rendering` is active, so no checker rule fires and there is no correct answer sitting unused. Both stages are silent. Saga #811's stated mechanism ("`check()` computes the right answer and `execute()` never consults it") is therefore true of shape A only — measured here rather than assumed. Form under test: `when <command> [ … ]` — the handler is never registered. `turtle-rendering` is load-bearing in this fixture's declared profile set rather than decorative: without it `forward` would itself be flagged and the empty expectation would be right for the wrong reason.
